html:
Adolf Hitler was the dictator of Germany from 1933 to 1945, the leader of the Nazi Party who started the Second World War in Europe and ordered the Holocaust. He was born in Austria in 1889 and served as a soldier in the German army in the First World War.

Germany's defeat in 1918, and the economic crises that followed, gave his movement its chance. He tried to seize power in Munich in 1923, failed, and wrote Mein Kampf in prison. In the Great Depression his party became the largest in the Weimar Republic, and he was named chancellor in January 1933. Within months he had banned other parties and made himself dictator of Nazi Germany.

  • He rearmed Germany and took Austria and the Sudetenland in 1938.
  • He made a pact with Stalin in August 1939, then invaded Poland on 1 September, which began the war in Europe.
  • He invaded the Soviet Union in 1941, the largest land campaign of the world wars.

Behind the front, his regime carried out the Holocaust: the murder of about six million Jews, along with Roma, disabled people, Soviet prisoners of war and many others. As Soviet troops closed in on Berlin, he killed himself in his bunker on 30 April 1945. Germany surrendered a week later.
